Start URLs

startUrls

Optional

Add Tweet, profile, search, or List URLs as strings or {"url":"..."} objects. Profile URLs may use /with_replies, /media, or best-effort /likes. For example, ["https://x.com/elonmusk", "https://x.com/search?q=AI"].

Type:array

Search query

twitterContent

Optional

Search query using X advanced search syntax. Supports keywords, hashtags, exact phrases, boolean operators, and date or Unix time windows. Every returned tweet falls inside your dates. For example, web scraping OR #datascience.

Type:string
Example:
web scraping OR #datascience

Search terms

searchTerms

Optional

Run multiple searches in one Actor run. Max Items applies across the run. Every result matches the date and Unix time operators in its term. For example, from:elonmusk AI, #bitcoin lang:en.

Type:string[]
Example:
[
  "from:elonmusk AI",
  "#bitcoin lang:en"
]

X handles

twitterHandles

Optional

X usernames whose posts to collect. Profile Tweets returns posts, reposts & the author's replies to their own posts. Add Exclude replies under Tweet type filters for original posts only. Profile With Replies keeps target-authored posts and replies. Add usernames with or without @. For example, elonmusk, @nasa.

Type:string[]
Example:
[
  "elonmusk",
  "@nasa"
]

Profile URLs

profileUrls

Optional

Alias for Start URLs. Add profile URL strings or {"url":"..."} objects.

Type:array

Tweet IDs

tweetIds

Optional

Tweet IDs or tweet URLs to look up directly. The run skips any other entry at no charge. Other sources in the same input run too, and Max Items applies across the run. There is no fixed ID count cap. For example, 20.

Type:string[]
Example:
[
  "20"
]

List IDs

listIds

Optional

X List IDs whose posts to collect. It is usually much faster than List URLs or the List ID filter below. For example, 1748648376080666720.

Type:string[]
Example:
[
  "1748648376080666720"
]

Mode

mode

Optional

Auto picks a mode from your input. Choose a mode to force one. Profile Tweets returns posts, reposts & the author's replies to their own posts. Profile With Replies keeps target-authored posts and replies. Profile Mentions returns posts that mention each handle, newest first. Translation returns X's translation of each Tweet. Embed HTML returns the markup that embeds each Tweet. Top tweets returns the tweets X ranks highest by 1 metric over a day, week or month. Tweet modes without Tweet IDs use Search when query input is present.

Type:string
Default:legacy
Options:
legacytweettweetssearchprofileTweetsprofileRepliesprofileMediaprofileLikesprofileMentionslistTweetsarticlerepliesquotesthreadretweetersfavoriterstranslationembedtopTweets

Max items

maxItems

Optional

Optional result cap across the whole run. Leave empty to use your Apify max total charge as the result limit when set. Without a spend cap, Xquik uses its built-in default. The Apify pricing box shows the current per-result price before the run starts. Diagnostic rows count toward this cap. The form starts at 1,000. A run can return 100,000 rows & more, so raise it for a full export.

Type:integer
Minimum:1
Default:100000

Max items per target

maxItemsPerTarget

Optional

Optional cap for each target in multi-target modes.

Type:integer
Minimum:1

Sort by

queryType

Optional

Latest returns newest first. Top is ranked by relevance and is not exhaustive. Latest + Top returns both without duplicates and fills your limit from either. Account timelines ignore this setting.

Type:string
Default:Latest
Options:
LatestTopLatest + Top

Output variant

outputVariant

Optional

Legacy preserves compatibility. Rich adds normalized public fields. Raw snapshot also adds a sanitized source snapshot. Compact and Full are Legacy aliases.

Type:string
Default:legacy
Options:
legacyrichrawcompactfull

Field style

fieldStyle

Optional

Controls top-level and nested field names for rich and raw results, including reply diagnostics. Use camelCase for JavaScript and TypeScript. Use snake_case for Python, SQL, CSV, and warehouses. Legacy output ignores this setting. Raw snapshots keep source names. Dataset views select columns only. They do not rename data.

Type:string
Default:legacy
Options:
legacycamelCasesnake_case

Output preset

outputPreset

Optional

Nested preserves the current object shape. Flat + nested also adds CSV-friendly author and media URL fields.

Type:string
Default:nested
Options:
nestedflat

Tag each result with its search term

includeSearchTerms

Optional

Attach the first matching search term as searchTerm on each unique Tweet. Use it to identify which query produced each deduplicated result.

Type:boolean
Default:false

Respect profile subpages

respectProfileSubpages

Optional

Honor profile subpage paths such as /with_replies, /media, and /likes in profile URLs. /with_replies returns target-authored posts and replies. The Actor excludes conversation context from other authors.

Type:boolean
Default:false

Since date

since

Optional

Keep posts from this date onward. Write YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS_UTC for a time of day. 31/01/2026 & 01/31/2026 also work. A date that fits both orders reads month first, so 04/01/2026 is 1 April. The Actor checks each post's date. For example, 2026-01-01_00:00:00_UTC.

Type:string

Until date

until

Optional

Keep posts from before this date. It takes the same date forms as Since date. The Actor checks each post's date. For example, 2026-04-01_00:00:00_UTC.

Type:string

Since time

since_time

Optional

Keep posts from this Unix time onward, in seconds. An ISO 8601 time such as 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z works too. The Actor checks each post's time. For example, 1704067200.

Type:string

Until time

until_time

Optional

Keep posts from before this Unix time, in seconds. An ISO 8601 time such as 2024-04-01T00:00:00Z works too. The Actor checks each post's time. For example, 1711929600.

Type:string

Within time

within_time

Optional

Only include tweets from the last N days, hours, minutes or seconds. Put d, h, m or s after the number. For example, 12h.

Type:string

since_id

Only include tweets with an ID greater than (posted after) this tweet ID.

Type:string

Only include tweets with an ID less than (posted before) this tweet ID.

Fields to keep

fields

Optional

Keep only these fields in each row. Pick names or type your own. Use a dot for a field inside an object, such as author.id. Columns arrive in the order & spelling you write. Every row keeps its id. Leave empty for every field. The price per row stays the same. A wrong name stops the run before it reads, at no charge. If names cannot be checked, the run reads on & lists unseen names last.

Type:string[]

Fields to drop

omitFields

Optional

Drop these fields & keep the rest. Every row keeps its id.

Type:string[]

Rename fields

renameFields

Optional

Give a field a new column name. The key is the field. The value is the new name. A renamed field becomes a top-level column.

Type:array

Flat columns

flatten

Optional

Turn each nested object into top-level columns, such as authorId. Lists stay lists. Use it for CSV & spreadsheets.

Type:boolean
Default:false

Fill missing fields with null

fillMissingFields

Optional

With Fields to keep, a field a row lacks arrives as null. Every row then has the same columns. Turn it off to leave such fields out.

Type:boolean
Default:true

Lists to join

joinFields

Optional

Turn each of these lists into 1 text value. Use it for CSV cells.

Type:string[]

Join separator

joinSeparator

Optional

Text between the items of a joined list.

Type:string
Default:,

Constant columns

constantFields

Optional

Add a column with the same text on every row. The key is the column name, such as campaign. The value is its text.

Type:array
